properties.line: Atlantic and Great Western: Salamanca – Dayton

segments.note: Built from three merging railroads (based in Jamestown NY, Meadville PA, and Franklin Mills/Kent OH) planning a 'Great Broad Route' since an 1852 Cleveland meeting. Construction from Salamanca reached Jamestown Sept 11, 1860, Corry May 27, 1861, and Meadville Nov 10, 1862; the full 388-mile Salamanca-Dayton line was completed during the Civil War (by ~1864) - the only major railroad built during the war. Reorganized as the New York, Pennsylvania and Ohio Railroad in 1880, then leased in 1883 to the New York, Lake Erie and Western Railroad (renamed Erie Railroad in 1895). Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Operated by the New York, Lake Erie and Western Railroad from 1883, renamed Erie Railroad in 1895. The Erie was always Jamestown's most important railroad, offering connections to New York City and Chicago; the city's grand final depot opened 1931. Frequency estimated, unsourced. The Erie ceased to exist October 17 1960, merging with the DL&W to form the Erie Lackawanna - the post-merger years are drawn as erie-salamanca-jamestown-dayton-el.

segments.note: Erie Lackawanna from the merger of October 17 1960 (Erie Lackawanna Railway from the 1968 reorganization). Passenger service to Jamestown wound down through the decade - the Atlantic Express/Pacific Express was cut in 1965, and the Lake Cities made the last passenger run in January 1970, a year before Amtrak existed. Jamestown has had no intercity passenger rail since. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

metadata.note: The Atlantic & Great Western Railway -- a 6-foot broad gauge line built during the Civil War to extend the Erie Railroad's broad gauge west from Salamanca, NY to Dayton, OH -- and its Erie Railroad successor. The route now follows the company's own station list: Salamanca - Randolph - Jamestown - Ashville - Corry - Union City - Cambridge Springs - Meadville - Greenville - Orangeville - Warren - Ravenna - Kent - Akron - Wadsworth - Ashland - Mansfield - Galion - Marion - Richwood - Urbana - Springfield - Dayton, 388 miles from Salamanca. The A&GW was three companies chartered separately in three states (the Erie & New York City Railroad at Jamestown, the Meadville Railroad in Pennsylvania, and the Franklin & Warren Railroad at Franklin Mills -- now Kent -- in Ohio) and worked as one line; broad-gauge cars reached Akron on 18 November 1863 and Dayton on 20 June 1864, where the connection with the Cincinnati, Hamilton & Dayton gave a continuous 6-foot gauge route from New York to St. Louis. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not from real timetables.
sources: https://archive.org/stream/atlanticgreatwes00simm/atlanticgreatwes00simm_djvu.txt ('The Atlantic and Great Western Railway: connections, stations, distances, map, &c.', the company's own guide). Used for the complete main-line station list and mileages from Salamanca that the route geometry now follows: Red House 7, Steamburg 12, Randolph 18, Kennedy 25, Levant 30, Jamestown 34, Ashville 41, Panama 48, Bear Lake 50, Columbus 58, Corry 61, Union 72, Mill Village 79, Cambridge 88, Venango 92, Saegertown 97, Meadville 103, Evansburg 115, Adamsville 121, Greenville 129, Orangeville 142, Burghill 144, Baconsburg 154, Warren 162, Leavittsburg 165, Braceville 169, Windham 174, Freedom 179, Ravenna 185, Kent 192, Tallmadge 198, Akron 202, Wadsworth 216, Seville 226, West Salem 238, Polk 245, Ashland 252, Mansfield 269, Ontario 276, Galion 284, Caledonia 295, Marion 305, Richwood 319, North Lewisburg 339, Urbana 353, Springfield 366, Enon 372, Osborn 378, Dayton 388. The same guide describes the line running 'westwardly through Meadville, Pa., Warren, Kent, Akron, and Galion to Dayton, O.' and records Kent as formerly called Franklin Mills and the home of Marvin Kent, first president of the A&GW in Ohio.

metadata.rule4_split_2026_08_24: Rule 4 ownership split. The Erie Railroad and the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western did not become one another -- they merged on October 17 1960 into a new company, the Erie Lackawanna Railroad (reorganized as the Erie Lackawanna Railway in 1968 under the Dereco holding company, and folded into Conrail April 1 1976). Before this pass the post-1960 years were still drawn in the predecessors' own colours, so one company appeared on the map in two different colours -- ex-Erie segments in Erie black #22223B, ex-Lackawanna in DL&W brown #7F5539. Every feature whose segments ran past 1960 has been split at the merger date into a second feature with identical geometry, company 'Erie Lackawanna Railroad', colour #A02C5A. Six features across six files: erie-mainline-jerseycity-buffalo, dlw-hoboken-scranton-buffalo, erie-salamanca-jamestown-dayton, erie-chicago-extension, erie-buffalo-niagara-falls, cmv-cleveland-youngstown. The NYS&W (nysw-jerseycity-stroudsburg) is deliberately NOT included -- it had reverted to independent operation by 1940 and was not part of the merger.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
